points: Vietnam veterans suffered problems upon their return to the US.
The Vietnam War caused the US public to lose faith in their government.
The Vietnamese people and landscape suffered greatly due to the war.
Although all of Indochina became communist, no other Southeast Asian country did.
Relations between the US and the USSR and China improved, which made nuclear war less likely.
keywords: have a strong effect on someone or something
a veteran is a person who has served in the armed forces

1654.correction: There are more than 45 000 different Christian denominations around the world today: although most of them believe the same fundamental things, there are stark differences between many of them.

886.belief: Catholic priests have never been allowed to get married.
886.statement: Catholic priests have never been allowed to get married.
886.correction: Catholic priests today are not allowed to get married, but in the past a great many were, even though it went against their rules. Some popes even had wives and children!

2356.belief: Different religious denominations believe very different things from each other.
2356.statement: Different religious denominations believe very different things from each other.
2356.correction: Different denominations within a religion will almost certainly believe the same fundamental things about their religion, but will differ over the details of belief or liturgy.

577.belief: Because the Abbasid Caliphate was large, the caliphs must have retained a lot of power.
577.statement: Because the Abbasid Caliphate was large, the caliphs must have retained a lot of power.
577.correction: Remind pupils that the caliphs had little effective power beyond Baghdad itself by the 11th century and the Seljuks became de facto rulers.

5989.belief: All medieval Islamic states must have been identical to one another.
5989.statement: Pupils assume that all medieval Islamic states must have been identical to one another.
5989.correction: Islamic states had similarities and differences (i.e. Cordoba had many Mediterranean influences; Persian influence was stronger in Baghdad).

4792.belief: As a Muslim island, there was little diversity in 11th century Sicily.
4792.statement: As a Muslim island, there was little diversity in 11th century Sicily.
4792.correction: Sicily was amongst the most diverse places in Eurasia during the 11th century with a population of Muslims, Christians and Jews.

9863.belief: 'eyewitness' accounts produce a more reliable picture of historical events.
9863.statement: Students may think that 'eyewitness' accounts produce a more reliable picture of historical events.
9863.correction: Although 'eyewitness' accounts are valuable, they were produced for a particular purpose which may distort their contents.

566.belief: The Bayeux Tapestry is a 'biased' source and therefore not useful to historians.
566.statement: That the Bayeux Tapestry is a 'biased' source and therefore not useful to historians.
566.correction: Although all sources were produced in a particular context, historians can ask careful questions of them to learn about the past.

9843.belief: 'the Church' is a physical building in which people pray.
9843.statement: Students might think that 'the Church' is a physical building in which people pray.
9843.correction: Explain that 'the Church' refers to the wider organisation of the Christian faith, including all buildings and people which belong to it.

11169.belief: The written word is the only useful source for the study of the past.
11169.statement: The written word is the only useful source for the study of the past.
11169.correction: Although written sources are useful, material remains can reveal much about past societies - it depends on the questions historians ask of the source.

8165.belief: Power associated with land ownership was a Norman import to England.
8165.statement: Pupils may think that power associated with land ownership was a Norman import to England.
8165.correction: Remind pupils that Anglo-Saxon England was a society largely based on land ownership and the power that this brought.

6314.statement: Pupils may consider sources to be inherently useful or not useful and make statements about bias.
6314.correction: Remind pupils that all sources are useful for investigating something, and that the questions we ask of them are important in this process.

10364.belief: Towns and cities are called by the same name as they were given when they were founded.
10364.statement: Towns and cities are called by the same name as they were given when they were founded.
10364.correction: Towns and cities all over the world have changed their name repeatedly for a wide variety of reasons. For example, York was called Eboracum by the Romans, Eoforwick by the Saxons and Jorvik by the Vikings!

4534.belief: The medieval Islamic world was a single entity.
4534.statement: The medieval Islamic world was a single entity.
4534.correction: The Islamic Empire started as a single entity, but by the 11th century had fragmented into several competing nations.

5701.belief: The pope has always been the most powerful person in the Roman Catholic Church.
5701.statement: The pope has always been the most powerful person in the Roman Catholic Church.
5701.correction: For much of the medieval period, a power struggle between the pope and local kings took place for control of religion within each country. In the early medieval period the pope had very little power at all.

8805.belief: Records of speeches from previous time periods are accurate representations of what these people actually said.
8805.statement: Records of speeches from previous time periods are accurate representations of what these people actually said.
8805.correction: Accurate recording of speeches was not a priority for many historians or record keepers up until fairly recently. It was seen as acceptable to put words into the mouths of past people based on what happened after or to reflect present sensibilities.

1658.belief: Christians 'saved' the Holy Land from barbaric Muslim conquerors.
1658.statement: Christians 'saved' the Holy Land from barbaric Muslim conquerors.
1658.correction: Muslims had generally treated Christians very well during the 400 or so years that they had controlled the Holy Land. In contrast, when the Christian crusaders arrived in the Holy Land they engaged in barbaric acts.

8786.belief: The only reason why crusaders went on the First Crusade was to capture Jerusalem for Christianity.
8786.statement: The only reason why crusaders went on the First Crusade was to capture Jerusalem for Christianity.
8786.correction: People went on crusade for a wide variety of reasons; for some people, capturing Jerusalem from the Muslims was important, but it was almost certainly not the reason why the First Crusade was called in the first place.

3617.belief: It has always been illegal for children to get married.
3617.statement: It has always been illegal for children to get married.
3617.correction: Throughout history, royal children were regularly betrothed at a young age in order to secure alliances between nations. Marriage followed later when the children had grown up, although they regularly still married younger than we do today.

11044.belief: Women were forbidden from ruling in their own right in England during the medieval period.
11044.statement: Women were forbidden from ruling in their own right in England during the medieval period.
11044.correction: The first time the concept of a woman ruling in her own right in England occurred it took everyone by surprise. No one had considered that a woman might rule alone, so there was no law preventing it from happening.

11042.belief: Women in England were not allowed to fight in wars.
11042.statement: Women in England were not allowed to fight in wars.
11042.correction: We have many examples of women leading the defence of castles throughout English history, and occasionally leading the attack on enemy territory as well. It was uncommon, but not unheard of.

5089.belief: Once a king dies or is taken prisoner, that is the end of the war.
5089.statement: Once a king dies or is taken prisoner, that is the end of the war.
5089.correction: Although a king is very important, there are many examples throughout history of a king's followers continuing to fight on successfully after their leader has been killed or captured.

550.belief: Barons must obey the their monarch's orders.
550.statement: Barons must obey the their monarch's orders.
550.correction: Although this is true in theory, in reality the barons and their monarch worked as a partnership: the monarch relied upon the barons and if they weren't doing a good enough job, they could expect to lose the support of their barons.

10070.belief: Surnames have always been used and they generally aren't changed from one generation to the next.
10070.statement: Surnames have always been used and they generally aren't changed from one generation to the next.
10070.correction: During the medieval period, people went by their first name and one or more given names. These given names could be nicknames based on their place of origin or occupation or a distinguishing feature. Some people chose their own given names.

3147.belief: France existed as a unified nation.
3147.statement: That France existed as a unified nation.
3147.correction: "Modern-day France" did not exist yet, instead the area we know as France, was actually a collection of separate lands/duchies.

3507.belief: History is not relevant to today.
3507.statement: History is not relevant to today.
3507.correction: Henry II’s reforms to the English legal system established the foundation of English common law, still in use today.

4535.belief: Medieval and modern Church power is equivalent.
4535.statement: Medieval and modern Church power is equivalent.
4535.correction: Explicitly outline the Church's organisational power: land ownership, clergy social status, and spiritual authority.

4763.belief: The murder of Thomas Becket was the undoing of Henry II.
4763.statement: The murder of Thomas Becket was the undoing of Henry II.
4763.correction: Long-term it increased Henry’s control over the Church. Bishops’ opposition decreased, while the Pope gave support after 1172.

4539.correction: Eleanor was an intelligent and powerful queen, acted as regent, and was a key conspirator of the revolt.

9926.belief: The role of the medieval monarch is comparable with today's monarchy.
9926.statement: Students may think that the role of the medieval monarch is comparable with today's monarchy.
9926.correction: A medieval king was judged by his ability on the battlefield. Success in battle was the best way for a king to become powerful.

3954.correction: King John inherited the Angevin Empire which stretched across England and France.

3955.belief: King John signed the Magna Carta.
3955.statement: King John signed the Magna Carta.
3955.correction: A modern misconception is that King John signed Magna Carta, this is untrue, royal documents were not signed but sealed.

3960.belief: All kings are adults and are the ultimate decision makers.
3960.statement: All kings are adults and are the ultimate decision makers.
3960.correction: Henry III became king when he was nine-years-old. As he was too young, regents were appointed to rule on Henry’s behalf.

4954.belief: The nobility in England identified as English.
4954.statement: The nobility in England identified as English.
4954.correction: This period marks a time when the nobility, who had their ancestral roots in France, had now come to see themselves as English.

5323.belief: Parliament is a powerful organisation that rules the country.
5323.statement: Parliament is a powerful organisation that rules the country.
5323.correction: At this point in history, the role of parliament was to advise the king.

4341.belief: Magna Carta was a singular event which resulted in a powerless monarchy and human rights for all.
4341.statement: Magna Carta was a singular event which resulted in a powerless monarchy and human rights for all.
4341.correction: Magna Carta started a process of struggle. The medieval monarchy remained powerful, and it did not grant freedoms to everybody.

3857.belief: Involving Parliament with the rule of the land meant there would be more fairness and justice.
3857.statement: Involving Parliament with the rule of the land meant there would be more fairness and justice.
3857.correction: Parliament passed discriminatory laws: handing more power to parliament did not necessarily mean a growth in rights and freedoms for all.

738.belief: Britain and England are terms which describe the same area.
738.statement: Britain and England are terms which describe the same area.
738.correction: Britain is the name for England, Scotland, and Wales.

10978.belief: The Welsh resistance was always a unified movement.
10978.statement: The Welsh resistance was always a unified movement.
10978.correction: Many Welsh princes cooperated with Edward's Welsh campaign in 1277. Edward’s army also included 9000 Welsh soldiers.

2592.belief: Edward I always intended to conquer Scotland and add it to his kingdom.
2592.statement: Edward I always intended to conquer Scotland and add it to his kingdom.
2592.correction: Edward I's initial aim was to have the Scottish pay him homage as their overlord.

9670.belief: The English army only comprised English soldiers.
9670.statement: Students may assume that the English army only comprised English soldiers.
9670.correction: The English forces also included Welsh and even some Scottish soldiers. This reflects the complex political and military alliances of the time.

600.belief: There is a belief that Edward I's military strength alone was sufficient to ensure long-term control and unity of Britain.
600.statement: There is a belief that Edward I's military strength alone was sufficient to ensure long-term control and unity of Britain.
600.correction: Edward I's approach was often brutal leading to ongoing resistance and ultimately limiting his ability to achieve lasting unification.

5419.belief: All people in the medieval period completed the same type of work as one another.
5419.statement: That all people in the medieval period completed the same type of work as one another.
5419.correction: Remind students that a wide range of different jobs and industries existed in medieval Norwich, even after it focused more on wools.

3724.belief: Increased powers of self government in Norwich gave all locals more control over decision-making.
3724.statement: Increased powers of self government in Norwich gave all locals more control over decision-making.
3724.correction: Only freemen had real political power in Norwich but very few women and almost no poor people were able to become freemen.

9889.belief: Medieval churches only focused on prayer and religious services.
9889.statement: Students think that medieval churches only focused on prayer and religious services.
9889.correction: Remind pupils that the Cathedral and other groups of churchmen in medieval Norwich also provided charity, education and hospital care.

11046.belief: All women in medieval Norwich had the same experience as one another.
11046.statement: All women in medieval Norwich had the same experience as one another.
11046.correction: Female experiences were varied, especially by wealth and social class. Those from wealthier backgrounds were more likely to be literate.

5693.belief: The poor always accepted their position in medieval society.
5693.statement: The poor always accepted their position in medieval society.
5693.correction: The poor challenged the social order in Norwich violently in 1381 and had to be actively managed by the elites.

5423.belief: All people from the same social group had the same experiences.
5423.statement: All people from the same social group had the same experiences.
5423.correction: Experiences could vary even between people from the same social group, especially if there were differences between their wealth and class.

3298.belief: The Ghana Empire was located in the modern-day country of Ghana.
3298.statement: The Ghana Empire was located in the modern-day country of Ghana.
3298.correction: The Ghana Empire was located in the Sahel, north of the Niger River, which is nowhere near the modern-day country of Ghana.

3066.belief: All followers of the same religion practise their religion in the same way.
3066.statement: All followers of the same religion practise their religion in the same way.
3066.correction: There are often large differences between followers of the same religion: people include elements of their own culture in their worship.

2643.belief: Empires have to own land in order to control it.
2643.statement: Empires have to own land in order to control it.
2643.correction: Control can be gained through a variety of indirect means, such as through trade or tribute.

4794.belief: Muslims mainly live in the Middle East.
4794.statement: Muslims mainly live in the Middle East.
4794.correction: Islam is the second most popular religion in the world, with Muslim-majority countries spread as far as Morocco in the west to Indonesia in the east.

3661.belief: It is impossible for large numbers of people to cross the Sahara Desert.
3661.statement: It is impossible for large numbers of people to cross the Sahara Desert.
3661.correction: Although extremely dangerous, the Sahara Desert has been crossed many times by large groups of people. Large amounts of provisions are needed though, which is why it is not a common occurrance.

10037.belief: Successful empires dominate and subjugate the conquered people within the empire in order to keep them loyal.
10037.statement: Successful empires dominate and subjugate the conquered people within the empire in order to keep them loyal.
10037.correction: The Mali aristocracy adopted a successful 'hands off' approach to governance, allowing the different kingdoms within the empire a great degree of autonomy.

9287.belief: Only silk was traded along the Silk Road.
9287.statement: Only silk was traded along the Silk Road.
9287.correction: Silk was a primary commodity for a long time along the Silk Road, but there were many different goods and ideas that were traded between East and West along the trade route.

681.belief: The Black Death only affected Europe.
681.statement: The Black Death only affected Europe.
681.correction: European records from the time are numerous and detailed, so we have a very clear idea about the impact of the Black Death on Europe. However, the Black Death affected a large geographic area, including places without detailed records of the impact.

682.belief: The Black Death was a terrible one-off event.
682.statement: The Black Death was a terrible one-off event.
682.correction: Although the Black Death was a one-off event, the plague, the disease that was the Black Death, continued to afflict Europe for hundreds of years after it first came to Europe in the 14th century.

3500.correction: This will be addressed across the course of the unit, but within this lesson it is worth drawing attention to the competing causes listed in the discussion of the Peasants' Revolt.

9603.belief: The Statute of Labourers immediately forced all peasants to return to their home manors and to cease negotiating higher wages.
9603.statement: That the Statute of Labourers immediately forced all peasants to return to their home manors and to cease negotiating higher wages.
9603.correction: Through the interpretations section of the lesson, draw out the point that the Statute of Labourers was unenforceable in many cases.

4536.belief: Medieval people called their social system 'the feudal system'.
4536.statement: Medieval people called their social system 'the feudal system'.
4536.correction: In fact, the term feudal system or feudalism did not start to be used until the 17th century.

5429.belief: People at the time called the conflict the Hundred Years' War.
5429.statement: People at the time called the conflict the Hundred Years' War.
5429.correction: People at the time would not have known how long the wars were going to last, so this name came after the conflict had ended.

8933.belief: Revolts and rebellions are driven purely by rage and frustration.
8933.statement: Revolts and rebellions are driven purely by rage and frustration.
8933.correction: Most revolts and rebellions have a number of causes and are usually led by people with a plan and aims to achieve.

4350.belief: The main aim of the rebels in the Peasants' Revolt was to overthrow the king.
4350.statement: That the main aim of the rebels in the Peasants' Revolt was to overthrow the king.
4350.correction: In fact the rebels' grievances were against local officials and the king's advisers, who they believed were misleading the king into acting against the interests of his people.

9703.statement: Students may believed that the Yorkists and Lancastrians were from different families.
9703.correction: The Lancastrians and Yorkists were both part of the Plantagenet family.

601.belief: The belief that Margaret of Anjou was a vicious and unpleasant woman.
601.statement: The belief that Margaret of Anjou was a vicious and unpleasant woman.
601.correction: A woman who held power would have likely been criticised in the medieval period and Yorkists would also have wanted to show her in an unfavourable light.

9756.statement: Students may get confused between Edward, Prince of Wales and Edward IV.
9756.correction: Explain that Edward, Prince of Wales, is the only son of Henry VI and Margaret of Anjou, and a Lancastrian. Edward IV is the son of Richard, Duke of York, who became Edward IV, and a Yorkist.

9692.belief: The king could rule without the support ot the nobility.
9692.statement: Students might believe that the king could rule without the support ot the nobility.
9692.correction: Explain that the king relied on nobles to keep law and order in society, particularly in more remote parts of the kingdom.

9681.statement: Students may become confused by the number of historical figures that share the same name.
9681.correction: Ensure students can differentiate between Edward IV and Prince Edward.

9963.belief: The Wars of the Roses ended with the victory of Henry VII at Bosworth and that all historians agree with this interpretation.
9963.statement: Students may think the Wars of the Roses ended with the victory of Henry VII at Bosworth and that all historians agree with this interpretation.
9963.correction: Explain that Henry VII also faced rebellions at the start of his reign and, although the Tudors are well-known for their rule of England, few expected them to last long as a result of the rebellions and the prior decades of instability.

7986.belief: Many of the ideas of the Renaissance were new to science, literature and art.
7986.statement: Pupils may think that many of the ideas of the Renaissance were new to science, literature and art.
7986.correction: Explain to pupils that the Renaissance was a period during which knowledge lost in Western Europe was rediscovered, rather than created for the first time.

7655.belief: Because printing presses were mechanical, they were as fast and efficient as modern machinery.
7655.statement: Pupils might think that because printing presses were mechanical, they were as fast and efficient as modern machinery.
7655.correction: Explain to pupils that even though printing presses were much quicker than copying by hand, it could still take a relatively long time to print books.

7656.belief: Because Renaissance architects used mathematical calculations to design their buildings, these were without subsequent problems or issues.
7656.statement: Pupils might think that because Renaissance architects used mathematical calculations to design their buildings, these were without subsequent problems or issues.
7656.correction: Explain to pupils that these architects often made miscalculations and many subsequent improvement works were needed to ensure buildings like St Peter's did not fall down.

7771.belief: Dissection was banned by the medieval Catholic Church.
7771.statement: Pupils might think that dissection was banned by the medieval Catholic Church.
7771.correction: Explain to pupils that, while dissection was not banned, there was still a taboo around handling dead bodies which limited the number of dissections that took place during the medieval period.

7960.belief: We can learn little from imagery that has been produced for the purposes of propaganda.
7960.statement: Pupils may think that we can learn little from imagery that has been produced for the purposes of propaganda.
7960.correction: Explain to pupils that we can learn a lot from such imagery as it is a window into the minds of those who had it produced, and helps us to understand some of their concerns and motivations.

6135.belief: Some sources have a greater inherent value than others.
6135.statement: Pupils may believe that some sources have a greater inherent value than others.
6135.correction: Remind pupils that a source's value rests entirely upon the enquiry for which it is used and the questions asked of it. No source has inherent value unless used as part of an enquiry.

9340.belief: A single person cannot shape history by themselves.
9340.statement: A single person cannot shape history by themselves.
9340.correction: The Great Man Theory in History - the idea that a single person is responsible for important events - is somewhat outdated, but occasionally, as is the case with Martin Luther, an argument can be made that individuals can radically shape events.

5894.belief: Protestantism is a single unified religion.
5894.statement: Protestantism is a single unified religion.
5894.correction: There are, today, thousands of different Christian denominations that can be considered versions of Protestantism. Almost from its very inception, Protestantism split into a variety of competing belief systems.

3962.belief: Kings have the power to do whatever they want in their own countries.
3962.statement: Kings have the power to do whatever they want in their own countries.
3962.correction: For a great deal of English history, the power of the kings has been restricted by English laws and religious laws issued by the pope in Rome.

4031.belief: There has always been a large variety of names that people could be called.
4031.statement: There has always been a large variety of names that people could be called.
4031.correction: In societies that do not experience a great deal of immigration, the pool of names that people can be called can be limited. This was the case for hundreds of years in England, causing many people to share the same names (e.g. Thomas!).

5393.belief: People decide for themselves what religious beliefs they hold.
5393.statement: People decide for themselves what religious beliefs they hold.
5393.correction: For much of English history, people had to believe what the monarch told them to believe, else they would be killed. This insistence upon belief became more relaxed only in the relatively recent past.

5893.belief: The Protestant Reformation was a single event.
5893.statement: The Protestant Reformation was a single event.
5893.correction: The Protestant Reformation happened over a long period of time and happened differently in different countries. Some countries moved swiftly away from Catholic beliefs, whereas in others the pace of change was slower or even reverted backwards.

2628.belief: Elizabeth was the first female ruler of England.
2628.statement: Elizabeth was the first female ruler of England.
2628.correction: There were female rulers before Elizabeth, including her sister Mary I immediately preceeding her.

2799.belief: Everyone in Elizabethan England was Protestant.
2799.statement: Everyone in Elizabethan England was Protestant.
2799.correction: Protestantism in Elizabethan England was the norm by the end of Elizabeth's reign, but England was religiously divided during her reign.

4472.belief: Mary, Queen of Scots and 'Bloody Mary' were the same person.
4472.statement: Mary, Queen of Scots and 'Bloody Mary' were the same person.
4472.correction: The two Marys were cousins, not the same person. Mary was a very common name at this time.

2678.belief: The English navy destroyed the Spanish Armada.
2678.statement: The English navy destroyed the Spanish Armada.
2678.correction: Most of the ships lost from the Spanish Armada were sunk in storms after the battle against the English navy.

2629.belief: The Elizabethan period was a 'Golden Age'.
2629.statement: The Elizabethan period was a 'Golden Age'.
2629.correction: Whilst there were many positives that came about during the Elizabethan era, many people suffered from poverty and starvation.

3496.belief: Historians all agree about what happened in the past.
3496.statement: Historians all agree about what happened in the past.
3496.correction: Historians are constantly arguing and changing their minds about events in the past as new evidence comes to light.

3355.belief: The government is there to help people when they are in need.
3355.statement: The government is there to help people when they are in need.
3355.correction: Throughout much of history, governments have regularly failed to support the most vulnerable in society, as many of them did not see that as their function.

2929.belief: Farmers will not starve because they grow their own food.
2929.statement: Farmers will not starve because they grow their own food.
2929.correction: Poor harvests can put a great deal of strain on the amount of food a farmer can grow, even food for subsistence.

2677.belief: The English have always been a nation of animal lovers.
2677.statement: The English have always been a nation of animal lovers.
2677.correction: Blood sports were a very popular form of entertainment for hundreds of years. A large variety of animals were killed for our entertainment, such as bulls, bears and badgers.

3362.belief: Governments and societies have generally been sympathetic to people in extreme poverty who may have been reduced to begging.
3362.statement: Governments and societies have generally been sympathetic to people in extreme poverty who may have been reduced to begging.
3362.correction: Throughout much of history, there has been little sympathy for people in extreme poverty from the majority of governments and societies, even when the circumstances that drove people into poverty are clearly out of their own control.

4051.belief: Laws are regularly scrutinised and updated by the government.
4051.statement: Laws are regularly scrutinised and updated by the government.
4051.correction: Many laws remain unchanged and in place for an exceedingly long time. Sometimes new laws are created which make the old ones redundant, but other times there is no need to replace the existing law if it is still relevant.

3499.belief: Historians all study the same things in history.
3499.statement: Historians all study the same things in history.
3499.correction: There is a large and ever-growing variety of themes that historians look at in history that shape the way we view the past, e.g. military history, economic history, women's history and many more.

4826.belief: All Native American were the same and part of a single society.
4826.statement: All Native American were the same and part of a single society.
4826.correction: There was a wide range of indigenous nations in the Americas, with many differences between their sizes, social structure and cultures.

7611.belief: America was ‘discovered’ by Europeans or that it was a 'new' place.
7611.statement: Pupils think that America was ‘discovered’ by Europeans or that it was a 'new' place.
7611.correction: Remind pupils that there were long-established communities in the Americas before European arrival - they did not need to be discovered.

5981.belief: European settlement completely destroyed indigenous communities.
5981.statement: Pupils assume that European settlement completely destroyed indigenous communities.
5981.correction: Native Americans were devastated overall by European colonisation but indigenous communities persisted and were never completely overwhelmed.

7808.belief: England was a comparable colonial power to Spain in the 16th century.
7808.statement: Pupils think that England was a comparable colonial power to Spain in the 16th century.
7808.correction: English colonisation attempts began much later than Spain’s, and occurred on a much smaller-scale with less government involvement.

3921.belief: John Rolfe’s marriage to Pocahontas represented goodwill between colonists and the Powhatan tribe.
3921.statement: John Rolfe’s marriage to Pocahontas represented goodwill between colonists and the Powhatan tribe.
3921.correction: Pocahontas' marriage involved her capture and forced conversion to Christianity. Pocahontas was used by the English for their own advantage.

2768.belief: Europeans conquered the Americas easily because they had better weapons and technology.
2768.statement: Europeans conquered the Americas easily because they had better weapons and technology.
2768.correction: European diseases killed and weakened many Native Americans, undermining indigenous resistance to European conquest.

5321.belief: Parliament in the 17th century was similarly superior to the monarch as it is today.
5321.statement: Parliament in the 17th century was similarly superior to the monarch as it is today
5321.correction: Parliament was there to assist the monarch but they could rule without it and did not consider it an equal to themselves

5806.belief: Primary sources are inherently useful because they were published at the time of an event.
5806.statement: Primary sources are inherently useful because they were published at the time of an event.
5806.correction: Sources are produced for a variety of purposes which can affect what they say. Propaganda sources might falsify information to persuade.

5322.belief: Parliament fought both Civil Wars to remove Charles I from power.
5322.statement: Parliament fought both Civil Wars to remove Charles I from power
5322.correction: The majority of people in Parliament wanted to change how Charles I behaved but only a minority wanted to remove the king from power.

5324.belief: Parliament ruled the country for the whole Interregnum period.
5324.statement: Parliament ruled the country for the whole Interregnum period.
5324.correction: Parliament ruled the country at the start of the Interregnum but was dismissed, recomposed, and ruled without at other times after 1652.

8927.belief: The Restored monarchy acted exactly the same way as it had before the Civil War.
8927.statement: The Restored monarchy acted exactly the same way as it had before the Civil War
8927.correction: Charles II made a great effort to work with Parliament more co-operatively than his father. He let Parliament sit continuously for 18 years.

2001.belief: All contemporary sources can be accepted based solely on the value of their content.
2001.statement: That all contemporary sources can be accepted based solely on the value of their content.
2001.correction: Historians must consider how the provenance of a source may have affected the way it discusses and portrays a historical issue.

1265.belief: Only children of the monarch are next in line for the throne, not siblings.
1265.statement: Only children of the monarch are next in line for the throne, not siblings.
1265.correction: As Charles II did not have any legitimate children, his heir was his brother, James II.

4712.belief: Monarchs need to secure their positions by imprisoning or killing any claimants to the throne.
4712.statement: Monarchs need to secure their positions by imprisoning or killing any claimants to the throne.
4712.correction: Although many monarchs have acted in this way, there are countless examples of monarchs who tolerated the freedom of strong claimants to the throne in order to not appear despotic. William III of Orange is a good example.

9133.belief: All Scottish people at the time followed the same type of Protestantism.
9133.statement: All Scottish people at the time followed the same type of Protestantism.
9133.correction: Scotland at this time was experiencing a serious split in the Protestant religion between Episcopalians and Presbyterians. The Episcopalians supported James while the Presbyterians supported William III.

10989.belief: The 'Whigs' gained their name because of the fancy wigs and hairstyles that were the fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries.
10989.statement: The 'Whigs' gained their name because of the fancy wigs and hairstyles that were the fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries.
10989.correction: 'Whigs' has nothing to do with hairstyles, but was instead originally a derogatory term used to describe the 'Country Party', as they were originally known. 'Whig' was a sound Scottish drovers shouted when controlling cattle on the way to market.

3839.belief: Interpretations of history are set in stone.
3839.statement: Interpretations of history are set in stone.
3839.correction: Many aspects of history face regular revisions as more research is conducted.

5352.correction: Our understanding of the past changes frequently, which causes us to look at events in different ways. As such, how we view the past is constantly changing.

2766.belief: European merchants arrived in West Africa with the intention of starting to enslave people.
2766.statement: European merchants arrived in West Africa with the intention of starting to enslave people.
2766.correction: European merchants were attracted by the potential amount of gold they would be able to trade in West Africa.

5117.belief: No one challenged the Portuguese when they began buying enslaved people to take to the Americas.
5117.statement: No one challenged the Portuguese when they began buying enslaved people to take to the Americas.
5117.correction: Many rulers and local people in West Africa were opposed to the trading of enslaved people from the very beginning.

10433.belief: The triangular trade was a simple trading route with three main points.
10433.statement: The triangular trade was a simple trading route with three main points.
10433.correction: The triangular trade was a complex system of trade, that is often simplified to help us better understand it.

184.belief: All African kingdoms and rulers willingly participated in the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
184.statement: All African kingdoms and rulers willingly participated in the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
184.correction: Some kingdoms did cooperate, but many - like the Kingdom of Benin - also tried to resist by refusing to trade enslaved people.

742.belief: Britain was always involved in the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
742.statement: Britain was always involved in the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
742.correction: Britain became involved in the trade in the 1500s, initially selling enslaved people onto plantations in Spanish and Portuguese colonies.

3959.belief: All kingdoms in West Africa saw the same changes as a result of the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
3959.statement: All kingdoms in West Africa saw the same changes as a result of the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
3959.correction: Some kingdoms were weaker as a result of wars between kingdoms, others were weakened because of alliances and others continued to thrive.

5819.belief: Prior to the Mughal conquest, India was all ruled by a single state.
5819.statement: Prior to the Mughal conquest, India was all ruled by a single state.
5819.correction: Multiple states ruled over India prior to Babur's successful invasion from 1525-27. In northern India this included a mix of Muslim and Hindu-led states.

9672.belief: Political instability is only the result of foreign powers challenging the leaders of a country.
9672.statement: Students assume political instability is only the result of foreign powers challenging the leaders of a country.
9672.correction: Political instability at the start of Humayun's reign partly occurred because of rebellions by his younger brothers and political instability in the 1550s was created by descendants of Sher Shah fighting one another for power.

205.belief: Akbar is remembered as a strong military leader because he only used violence to expand the Mughal Empire.
205.statement: Akbar is remembered as a strong military leader because he only used violence to expand the Mughal Empire.
205.correction: Akbar used a variety of methods to expand the Mughal Empire. In some cases, such as to gain control over the Rajput states, diplomacy was more important for expansion under Akbar than violence.

206.belief: Akbar's religious tolerance was absolute throughout his reign.
206.statement: Akbar's religious tolerance was absolute throughout his reign.
206.correction: Akbar made some exceptions to his general policy of religious tolerance, such as when he declared a jihad against the Hindu Kingdom of Mewar.

2852.belief: Expansion of an empire always means that is growing stronger.
2852.statement: Expansion of an empire always means that is growing stronger.
2852.correction: As the Mughal Empire expanded, the costs of maintaining its rule across India also increased and new tensions were created with groups who lost out from extended Mughal control.

10877.belief: Violence was not important during the reign of some monarchs such as Akbar the Great.
10877.statement: Violence was not important during the reign of some monarchs such as Akbar the Great.
10877.correction: Violence was consistently part of the reigns of Mughal emperors. Akbar ordered the massacre of 30 000 people living in Mewar after they resisted the Mughal army in 1568.

739.belief: Only Britain and Europe engaged in empire building.
739.statement: Only Britain and Europe engaged in empire building.
739.correction: In fact, empires have existed across the world since at least the ancient period: several dynasties ruled across China, the Ottoman Empire spanned across Asia, Africa and Europe, and the Mali Empire controlled extensive territories in West Africa.

2641.correction: In fact, empire was often an ad-hoc private affair. For example, the East India Company had taken control over large parts of India - an expansion driven by opportunistic officials largely acting independently of the British government.

10382.belief: The Transatlantic Slave Trade made up a large percentage of Britain’s national income.
10382.statement: The Transatlantic Slave Trade made up a large percentage of Britain’s national income.
10382.correction: The direct profit from the trade in enslaved people was 1% of Britain’s national income. However, much more wealth was generated in Britain from the trade in products produced by enslaved labour, and by provisioning the Transatlantic Slave Trade.

2769.belief: Europeans were more powerful than other states and social groups in the 17th century.
2769.statement: Europeans were more powerful than other states and social groups in the 17th century.
2769.correction: Although European groups like the EIC were powerful, the Mughal Emperors retained greater power in the 17th century. Aurangzeb comprehensively defeated the EIC's military challenged during Child's War.

508.belief: Aurangzeb was completely intolerant towards and alienated all non-Muslims.
508.statement: Aurangzeb was completely intolerant towards and alienated all non-Muslims.
508.correction: Aurangzeb continued to support non-Muslim places of worship and to promote non-Muslim officials in the empire, leading to increased numbers of Hindus and Sikhs serving the Mughal Empire by the end of his reign.

10039.belief: The successor states completely ignored the Mughal Emperor's authority.
10039.statement: The successor states completely ignored the Mughal Emperor's authority.
10039.correction: Successor states took a lot of power for themselves but still claimed to be loyal to the Mughals.

2564.belief: The East India Company relied entirely on European soldiers.
2564.statement: The East India Company relied entirely on European soldiers.
2564.correction: The EIC increasingly recruited sepoy soldiers to serve in its army from the late-1740s onwards.

2608.belief: EIC victory in the Battle of Plassey only relied upon its own strengths.
2608.statement: EIC victory in the Battle of Plassey only relied upon its own strengths.
2608.correction: The EIC army benefitted from Indian support, including its secret agreement with Mir Jafar who refused to let his troops participate in the battle.

4752.belief: Mughal authority collapsed in the 17th century.
4752.statement: Mughal authority collapsed in the 17th century.
4752.correction: Mughal rule faced challenges, but the emperors still had enough military power and political control to maintain their authority during the 17th century.

13.belief: The 1701 Act of Settlement meant that parliament no longer needed to worry about a Catholic taking the throne in the future.
13.statement: The 1701 Act of Settlement meant that parliament no longer needed to worry about a Catholic taking the throne in the future.
13.correction: Although the 1701 Act of Settlement stipulated a Catholic or the spouse of a Catholic could never succeed to the throne of England, parliament remained worried that a succession crisis could still ensue if a monarch died childless.

10906.belief: Walpole created the role of Prime Minister and the idea of Cabinet.
10906.statement: Walpole created the role of Prime Minister and the idea of Cabinet.
10906.correction: Walpole's leadership saw him become de-facto Prime Minister and he formalised the idea of Cabinet which already existed in a loose, unofficial form.

2697.belief: All Enlightenment philosophers were atheists and rejected religion entirely.
2697.statement: All Enlightenment philosophers were atheists and rejected religion entirely.
2697.correction: Enlightenment philosophers wanted to reshape and redefine the role religion and the Church played in society.

2698.correction: Some Enlightenment thinkers promoted racist theories while others advocated for equality.

2205.belief: The Declaration of Independence was signed after the settlers defeated the British in the Revolutionary War.
2205.statement: The Declaration of Independence was signed after the settlers defeated the British in the Revolutionary War.
2205.correction: The Declaration of Independence was signed early on in the Revolutionary War and the US Constitution was signed after the war had concluded.

3162.belief: The French Revolution only occurred because of the Enlightenment.
3162.statement: The French Revolution only occurred because of the Enlightenment.
3162.correction: The French Revolution occurred for a myriad of reasons. These include causes such as the Enlightenment, the influence of the American Revolution, the lavish spending of the monarchy and their supposed indifference to the plight of the Third Estate.

3434.belief: All the Haitian rebels were enslaved people.
3434.statement: All the Haitian rebels were enslaved people.
3434.correction: Many of the Haitian rebels were free people.

2000.belief: All contemporary British thinkers were complete supporters of the French Revolution.
2000.statement: All contemporary British thinkers were complete supporters of the French Revolution.
2000.correction: Levels of support for the French Revolution amongst contemporary British thinkers varied.

8935.belief: Revolutionary ideas failed to spread from France to other European countries.
8935.statement: Revolutionary ideas failed to spread from France to other European countries.
8935.correction: Revolutionary ideas did spread to other European countries, but they did not cause any successful revolutions.

4812.belief: Napoleon only ever experienced success during this period, and was never defeated.
4812.statement: Napoleon only ever experienced success during this period, and was never defeated.
4812.correction: Napoleon faced military setbacks (particularly at sea) during this period, usually at the hands of the British.

4811.belief: Napoleon became Emperor of France after he seized power from the Directory in 1799.
4811.statement: Napoleon became Emperor of France after he seized power from the Directory in 1799.
4811.correction: Napoleon became First Consul after seizing power from the Directory, but did not crown himself Emperor of France until 1804.

4813.correction: Napoleon was exiled twice. The first time to Elba after his defeat in Russia. He escaped back to France and gained support from his old troops and took power once more. He was defeated at Waterloo and exiled for the final time to St Helena.

3152.belief: All French cartoons are complimentary of Napoleon and all British cartoons are critical of Napoleon.
3152.statement: All French cartoons are complimentary of Napoleon and all British cartoons are critical of Napoleon.
3152.correction: Many French cartoons were critical of Napoleon and many British cartoons were critical of the British government's response to his actions.

5436.belief: All the peoples who revolted in Saint-Domingue were enslaved people.
5436.statement: All the peoples who revolted in Saint-Domingue were enslaved people.
5436.correction: The revolutionaries of Saint-Domingue were comprised of a combination of enslaved people, free people of African descent and free indigenous people.

10363.belief: Toussaint L'Ouverture was fighting against the French during the entirety of the Haitian Revolution.
10363.statement: Toussaint L'Ouverture was fighting against the French during the entirety of the Haitian Revolution.
10363.correction: He first fought Saint-Domingue's ruling French elites and slave-owners. He then fought Spanish troops after invading Spain's territory on the island. He then defeated a British invasion and became Haiti's official governor until France betrayed him.

9060.belief: Sait-Domingue was independent from France under Toussaint L'Ouverture's leadership.
9060.statement: Sait-Domingue was independent from France under Toussaint L'Ouverture's leadership
9060.correction: Toussaint L'Ouverture was technically the French Governor of Saint-Domingue due to his leadership during the slave uprising there during the 1790s. His attempt to establish the colony as a free country though in 1801 was a step too far for Napoleon.

52.belief: Abolition of slavery in Britain and its colonies was a response to a single event.
52.statement: Abolition of slavery in Britain and its colonies was a response to a single event.
52.correction: Abolition of slavery in Britain and its colonies was a response to a number of events and an ever-growing public demand for change.

14.belief: The 1807 Slave Trade Act freed all enslaved people in the British Empire.
14.statement: The 1807 Slave Trade Act freed all enslaved people in the British Empire.
14.correction: The 1807 Slave Trade Act did not free all enslaved people in the British Empire, but did ban the buying, selling and transportation of enslaved individuals from that point forward.

3435.belief: The Haitian Revolution directly inspired the abolition of slavery everywhere.
3435.statement: The Haitian Revolution directly inspired the abolition of slavery everywhere.
3435.correction: The events of the Haitian Revolution strengthened Britain's abolitionist movement and helped France to initially abolish slavery in 1794; but under Napoleon the threat of enslavement returned.

9667.belief: The Agricultural Revolution was predominantly facilitated by changes in technology.
9667.statement: Students assume the Agricultural Revolution was predominantly facilitated by changes in technology.
9667.correction: Farming tech in common use didn't change much. Improvements in agriculture occurred mainly because of the use of new farming methods.

3769.belief: The Industrial Revolution was only about the use of steam power.
3769.statement: That the Industrial Revolution was only about the use of steam power.
3769.correction: Many key changes in the Industrial Revolution related to developments beyond the use of steam power, such as the exploitation of water power.

3767.belief: The Industrial Revolution led to a decline in living conditions across all parts of Britain.
3767.statement: The Industrial Revolution led to a decline in living conditions across all parts of Britain.
3767.correction: The decline in living conditions during the Industrial Revolution was generally confined to industrial towns and their poorest areas.

8741.belief: Radicals encouraged the use of violence to solve the problems that industrial workers faced.
8741.statement: Radicals encouraged the use of violence to solve the problems that industrial workers faced.
8741.correction: Radicals like Cobbett and Hunt emphaisised the importance of peaceful protests and the need to persuade government to extend voting rights.

817.belief: Most campaigners for reform like the BPU wanted all adults in Britain to be enfranchised.
817.statement: Most campaigners for reform like the BPU wanted all adults in Britain to be enfranchised.
817.correction: The BPU campaigned for tax-paying males to be enfranchised, which would have continued to exclude many poor workers as well as women.

3765.belief: The Industrial Revolution affected all aspects of life in Britain equally.
3765.statement: The Industrial Revolution affected all aspects of life in Britain equally.
3765.correction: The impact of the Industrial Revolution may be measured differently depending on which aspects of life historians focus their attention on.

11116.belief: All working class men gained the right to vote due to the 1867 and 1884 Reform Acts.
11116.statement: All working class men gained the right to vote due to the 1867 and 1884 Reform Acts.
11116.correction: As property qualifications remained in place, a significant proportion of working class adult men remained unable to vote even after 1884.

3587.belief: Ideas of racial superiority were the only justification for British imperialism.
3587.statement: Ideas of racial superiority were the only justification for British imperialism.
3587.correction: Cultural and religious beliefs such as a belief in the superiority of Christianity helped to justify an encourage British imperialism throughout the 19th century.

5341.belief: All parts of the British Empire were always governed directly by the British government.
5341.statement: All parts of the British Empire were always governed directly by the British government.
5341.correction: In the first half of the 19th century, India was ruled by the British East India Company, not by the British Government.

3363.belief: Governor Grant's reforms after the Morant Bay Rebellion reduced the problem of poverty for Black Jamaicans.
3363.statement: Governor Grant's reforms after the Morant Bay Rebellion reduced the problem of poverty for Black Jamaicans.
3363.correction: Grant tackled discrimination and other issues but did not provide the financial assistance needed to help many Black Jamaicans escape poverty.

753.belief: British victory in the Opium wars allowed it to conquer large areas of China and establish many new colonies.
753.statement: British victory in the Opium wars allowed it to conquer large areas of China and establish many new colonies.
753.correction: Hong Kong was gained as a new British colony but Britain used its victory in the Opium Wars to force the Qing empire to change its behaviour, rather than to create new colonies.

744.belief: Britain ruled over large areas of Africa throughout the 19th century.
744.statement: Britain ruled over large areas of Africa throughout the 19th century.
744.correction: British colonies were mainly confined to coastal areas in the first half of the 19th century. It was only later that British rule extended into the African interior.

3740.belief: The Indian and Jamaican rebellions triggered complete change in those colonies.
3740.statement: The Indian and Jamaican rebellions triggered complete change in those colonies.
3740.correction: Major changes were introduced after these rebellions although little was changed to address the problem of poverty in either Jamaica or India.

3391.belief: The Great Exhibition was located in the Crystal Palace.
3391.statement: The Great Exhibition was located in the Crystal Palace.
3391.correction: The Great Exhibition, which became known as the Crystal Palace, was located in Hyde Park.

8966.belief: The rise of Germany and the USA and the growth of nationalist movements in the late 19th century contributed to imperial decline.
8966.statement: The rise of Germany and the USA and the growth of nationalist movements in the late 19th century contributed to imperial decline.
8966.correction: The British Empire responded to this rise in anxiety by showcasing their supremacy at Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.

10429.belief: The trend of British imperial decline was caused by foreign policy and external threats.
10429.statement: The trend of British imperial decline was caused by foreign policy and external threats.
10429.correction: There is a link between foreign and domestic policy, both of which contributed to imperial decline.

2602.belief: The effects of decolonisation were positive for countries newly independent from the British Empire.
2602.statement: The effects of decolonisation were positive for countries newly independent from the British Empire.
2602.correction: For many newly independent nations, freedom brought many difficulties as well as benefits.

5738.belief: It is possible to view the British Empire as either a force for good or bad.
5738.statement: It is possible to view the British Empire as either a force for good or bad.
5738.correction: The enormity of the British Empire and number of individuals involved means that to attach a simple label to the British Empire is an impossible task.

3498.belief: Historians have finished debating the legacy of the British Empire.
3498.statement: Historians have finished debating the legacy of the British Empire.
3498.correction: Historians continue to debate the legacy of the British Empire as new information emerges.

10860.belief: Victorian women played no political role in Britain in the 19th century.
10860.statement: Victorian women played no political role in Britain in the 19th century.
10860.correction: Women were increasingly politically active in Britain, for example, through their involvement in the abolitionist movement and through their participation in trade unions, despite being unable to vote.

10044.belief: The suffrage movement always involved violent or illegal tactics as well as peaceful and legal ones.
10044.statement: The suffrage movement always involved violent or illegal tactics as well as peaceful and legal ones.
10044.correction: The early suffragist movement was committed to peaceful tactics, even among the so-called 'radical suffragists'.

10045.belief: Suffragists were the same as suffragettes.
10045.statement: Suffragists were the same as suffragettes.
10045.correction: One way for pupils to remember the difference is that the suffraGETtes wanted to GET things done - deeds not words.

740.belief: Britain was the first country to give women the right to vote.
740.statement: Britain was the first country to give women the right to vote.
740.correction: New Zealand was the first country in which women gained the right to vote, in 1893. Australia was the next, nine years later.

604.belief: The belief that all women supported the war, and that women were immediately involved in war work from 1914.
604.statement: The belief that all women supported the war, and that women were immediately involved in war work from 1914.
604.correction: Some women were pacifists and did not support the war effort. Women were only brought into the workforce from 1916 due to labour shortages.

10870.belief: The view that it was the work women did to support the war effort which gained them the right to vote.
10870.statement: The view that it was the work women did to support the war effort which gained them the right to vote.
10870.correction: Many people were convinced women should be entitled to vote before 1914; however, the violence of the suffragettes and the interruption of WW1 delayed this.

2809.belief: Everyone knew what was agreed by countries which had made alliances before the start of the war.
2809.statement: Everyone knew what was agreed by countries which had made alliances before the start of the war.
2809.correction: Explain that important parts of the alliance agreements were not made public so other countries did not know about them.

455.belief: The assassination of Ferdinand led to the inevitable, immediate outbreak of a global war.
455.statement: That the assassination of Ferdinand led to the inevitable, immediate outbreak of a global war
455.correction: The outbreak of the war was the result of a series of context-dependent events, including the Austrian ultimatum and the Schlieffen Plan

745.belief: The British army went into the war confidently, with a large number of troops.
745.statement: The British army went into the war confidently, with a large number of troops.
745.correction: The British army had no more than 700 000 men in August 1914, they would need to use mass recruitment and colonial armies.

3504.belief: Historically the contribution of colonial troops to the war effort has been overlooked.
3504.statement: Historically the contribution of colonial troops to the war effort has been overlooked.
3504.correction: Colonial troops made significant contributions to the war, both within Europe and across the world.

10916.belief: The war had very little impact on Ireland.
10916.statement: The war had very little impact on Ireland.
10916.correction: Irish calls for independence were delayed by the outbreak of war, and then further delayed in 1918.

3633.belief: The impact of WWI was limited to Europe, and those directly affected by the deaths of troops.
3633.statement: The impact of WWI was limited to Europe, and those directly affected by the deaths of troops.
3633.correction: The impact of WWI can be seen in Britain across different groups in society, but also within British colonies across the world.

9669.belief: All communists and socialists shared the same ideas.
9669.statement: Students assume all communists and socialists shared the same ideas.
9669.correction: Marx's ideas were interpreted differently by different groups of socialists. In Russia, this led to the split of the Social Democratic Party.

8936.belief: Revolutions always involve the execution of the previous leaders of government.
8936.statement: Revolutions always involve the execution of the previous leaders of government.
8936.correction: Although there was violence during the February Revolution, Tsar Nicholas II agreed to abdicate.

702.belief: The Bolsheviks revolutionary background meant that they were completely different to the tsar.
702.statement: The Bolsheviks revolutionary background meant that they were completely different to the tsar.
702.correction: The Bolsheviks treated opposition similarly to the tsar, using a secret police and re-introducing censorship.

5396.belief: People only died in the Russian Civil War as a direct result of the fighting.
5396.statement: People only died in the Russian Civil War as a direct result of the fighting.
5396.correction: Millions of ordinary Russians died as a result of methods like the Red Terror and War Communism used by the Reds during the war.

928.belief: Changes in the leadership of Russia led to complete change in the country's politics.
928.statement: Changes in the leadership of Russia led to complete change in the country's politics.
928.correction: Both tsarist rule and Communist rule led to severe restrictions on political freedoms, including use of secret police to remove opposition.

9674.statement: Students assume that revolutions lead to complete change.
9674.correction: Emphasise that there were significant changes in Russia after 1917 but similarities remained, such as the lack of freedom for opposition.

3511.belief: Hitler was always an unpopular dictator.
3511.statement: Hitler was always an unpopular dictator.
3511.correction: Hitler often attracted enthusiastic crowds to his speeches. By January 1933, the popularity of Hitler and the Nazi Party had turned into an electoral success.

10328.belief: At the time, everyone knew Hitler was a tyrant, so appeasement was clearly wrong.
10328.statement: At the time, everyone knew Hitler was a tyrant, so appeasement was clearly wrong.
10328.correction: The international community was divided. Many wanted to avoid a repeat of World War One. Furthermore, many thought that Germany had been treated harshly after WWI, and it seemed fair for Germany to take back some of its territory.

752.belief: British troops began fighting against Nazi Germany immediately after war was declared.
752.statement: British troops began fighting against Nazi Germany immediately after war was declared.
752.correction: For eight months, there was very limited British, French and German military land operation on the Western Front. This became known as the 'Phoney War'

9406.belief: The sole turning point of the Second World War was due to America being brought into the conflict.
9406.statement: That the sole turning point of the Second World War was due to America being brought into the conflict.
9406.correction: America's entry into the conflict was an important turning point, however, another significant turning point occurred with the first defeat of the Nazi army in the Soviet Union.

235.belief: America and Britain won the war by defeating the Nazis in Berlin.
235.statement: America and Britain won the war by defeating the Nazis in Berlin.
235.correction: The Soviets had pushed the Nazi army back across eastern Europe; four out of five German soldiers killed in WW2 were killed on the Eastern Front.

487.belief: The atomic bombs dropped on Japan only had immediate impacts.
487.statement: The atomic bombs dropped on Japan only had immediate impacts.
487.correction: The bombs had unprecedented destructive power. They sent out a shock wave that incinerated everything within a four-mile radius and in the weeks that followed, people died from radiation poisoning despite having survived the initial blast.

3518.belief: The Holocaust was confined to Germany.
3518.statement: The Holocaust was confined to Germany.
3518.correction: The Nazis and their collaborators murdered 6 million Jews from across Europe and aimed to eliminate Jews from the entire continent.

9251.belief: Shared Jewish heritage meant that all European Jews lived similar lives.
9251.statement: Shared Jewish heritage meant that all European Jews lived similar lives.
9251.correction: Jews made individuals choices and were affected by factors such as wealth which led to the Jewish population living many different types of lives.

4843.belief: Nazi antisemitism meant they were immediately violent towards Jews.
4843.statement: Nazi antisemitism meant they were immediately violent towards Jews.
4843.correction: Open violence as a part of Nazi persecution only became common in 1938.

3917.belief: Most Jews murdered during the Holocaust were killed in gas chambers in concentration camps.
3917.statement: Most Jews murdered during the Holocaust were killed in gas chambers in concentration camps.
3917.correction: Gas chambers were set up in specially constructed extermination camps for Jews and killed millions, but roughly half of all Holocaust victims were killed by other means.

3254.belief: Only German Nazis were involved in the Holocaust.
3254.statement: Only German Nazis were involved in the Holocaust.
3254.correction: Examples such as the Vel' d'Hiv Raid in France, carried out in 1942, show that other Europeans collaborated and helped to perpetrate the Holocaust.

8913.belief: Resistance always involves the use of violence.
8913.statement: Resistance always involves the use of violence.
8913.correction: Jews adopted many nonviolent forms of resistance. Actions like smuggling resisted Nazi attempts to starve Jews and continuing education secretly resisted Nazi attempts to destroy Jewish culture.

4062.belief: Leaders in the Lodz Ghetto made 'bad' choices for choosing to comply with German orders.
4062.statement: Leaders in the Lodz Ghetto made 'bad' choices for choosing to comply with German orders.
4062.correction: Leaders in the Lodz Ghetto, like many other Jews, faced multiple poor choices - or 'choiceless choices'. The decisions they made occurred in extreme circumstances where they had little real control over their own survival.

3867.belief: All Irish nationalists shared the same views and had the same aims.
3867.statement: All Irish nationalists shared the same views and had the same aims.
3867.correction: Some Irish nationalists wanted Home Rule for Ireland whereas other nationalists (known as republicans) wanted complete independence from Britain. After 1921, republicans split between those who supported the Anglo-Irish Treaty and those who did not.

708.belief: The borders drawn during Partition were clear and accepted by all.
708.statement: The borders drawn during Partition were clear and accepted by all.
708.correction: The Radcliffe Line, which demarcated the borders, was highly contentious and led to significant disputes and confusion, which resulted in violence.

741.belief: Britain has no historic role in the creation of tension between Arabs and Jews over Palestine.
741.statement: That Britain has no historic role in the creation of tension between Arabs and Jews over Palestine.
741.correction: Britain's colonial role in Palestine during and after the First World War involved it making conflicting promises to both Arabs and Jews over Palestine's future.

2207.belief: Decolonisation happened in a peaceful and orderly way in all of Britain's African colonies.
2207.statement: Decolonisation happened in a peaceful and orderly way in all of Britain's African colonies.
2207.correction: Decolonisation in many of Britain's African colonies was mostly peaceful; however, there were exceptions. For example, in Kenya there was significant violence as the British authorities used brutal measures to suppress the Mau Mau Uprising (1952-60).

869.belief: All Caribbean countries gained independence from Britain at the same time.
869.statement: All Caribbean countries gained independence from Britain at the same time.
869.correction: Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago were the first of Britain's Caribbean colonies to achieve independence in 1962, however, the last British colony in the Caribbean to gain independence was Saint Kitts and Nevis in 1983.

746.belief: The British Empire was different from other European empires because Britain willingly relinquished control of its colonies and decolonisation was mostly a peaceful process.
746.statement: The British Empire was different from other European empires because Britain willingly relinquished control of its colonies and decolonisation was mostly a peaceful process.
746.correction: While it was a peaceful process in some British colonies, decolonisation involved significant violence in other colonies. Even in colonies where decolonisation was relatively peaceful there was some violence (e.g., Accra Riots in the Gold Coast).

9660.statement: Students may aassume William Beveridge was a member of the Labour Party.
9660.correction: William Beveridge was actually a member of the Liberal Party.

2623.belief: Every element of the NHS was free for a considerable time after its creation.
2623.statement: Every element of the NHS was free for a considerable time after its creation.
2623.correction: Every element of the NHS was only free for a short time, as the overwhelming demand resulted in the need to introduce prescription fees.

8106.belief: The people had control of nationalised industries.
8106.statement: Pupils might think that the people had control of nationalised industries.
8106.correction: The first chairman of the National Coal Board (NCB) was the former owner of the largest coal company in Britain.

9788.statement: Students might not realise that women as well as men were conscripted during WW2.
9788.correction: In 1940, single women aged 20-30, and widowed women without children, were conscripted into war work.

9783.belief: Everyone the descendants of the Windrush generation had the automatic right to stay and work in Britain.
9783.statement: Students might presume that everyone the descendants of the Windrush generation had the automatic right to stay and work in Britain.
9783.correction: The children of Windrush generation did not have their own passports, and it was difficult to prove they had entered the UK legally. This led to the Windrush Scandal in 2018.

9698.belief: Rationing ended when the Second World War ended in 1945.
9698.statement: Students might believe rationing ended when the Second World War ended in 1945.

4541.belief: Medieval women completed no work other than housework and looking after children.
4541.statement: Medieval women completed no work other than housework and looking after children.
4541.correction: Although they were responsible for housework and childcare and did not have the same opportunities to work as men, women in the medieval period completed a range of other work; the type of work they completed was determined by where they lived.

2851.belief: The existence of female rulers like Elizabeth I and Mary, Queen of Scots, meant that women in early modern Britain had significantly more power than in the medieval period.
2851.statement: The existence of female rulers like Elizabeth I and Mary, Queen of Scots, meant that women in early modern Britain had significantly more power than in the medieval period.
2851.correction: It was extremely rare for women to wield power during this period. Early modern Britain was a patriarchal society in which society was controlled by men and the vast majority of women were excluded from all positions of power and influence.

4364.belief: The majority of women worked in factories throughout this period.
4364.statement: The majority of women worked in factories throughout this period.
4364.correction: The work women did and whether they worked at all was largely determined by class. From the mid-19th century, legislation placed restrictions on the type and amount of work women were able to do and the number of women working in factories decreased.

11029.belief: Winning the right to vote in 1919 led to a radical transformation in the status and position of women in society in the 1920s and 1930s.
11029.statement: Winning the right to vote in 1919 led to a radical transformation in the status and position of women in society in the 1920s and 1930s.
11029.correction: Although the Representation of the People Act of 1919 was a significant turning point, Britain in the 1920s and 1930s remained a very patriarchal society.

2714.belief: The Equal Pay Act (1970) led to women being paid the same as men.
2714.statement: The Equal Pay Act (1970) led to women being paid the same as men.
2714.correction: Although the Equal Pay Act made it illegal to pay women less than men for doing the same work, many employers adjusted job descriptions for female workers to avoid paying them equally.

11052.belief: Women's suffrage led to a rapid increase in the number of female MPs in Parliament.
11052.statement: Women's suffrage led to a rapid increase in the number of female MPs in Parliament.
11052.correction: By 1931, there were only 15 female MPs in Parliament; however, women's suffrage meant that MPs were more likely to support new laws that had a positive impact on the lives of women.

283.belief: Anglo-Saxon monarchs had to be great warriors to be made king.
283.statement: Anglo-Saxon monarchs had to be great warriors to be made king.
283.correction: In fact some monarchs, such as Edward the Confessor, were not warriors but instead very religious men whose faith inspired others.

282.belief: An Anglo-Saxon monarch had all the power.
282.statement: An Anglo-Saxon monarch had all the power.
282.correction: In fact, Anglo-Saxon nobles could force their monarchs to do things they did not want to do. For example, King Edward was forced to allow the House of Godwin back from exile and restore them to their earldoms.

4711.belief: After a monarch dies, their eldest child automatically becomes monarch after them.
4711.statement: After a monarch dies, their eldest child automatically becomes monarch after them.
4711.correction: In Anglo-Saxon England, an heir was always in a strong position, but even if there was an heir, the Witan could use their influence for someone else to be made monarch - if, for example, the heir was too young.

10351.belief: It took many weeks to travel from the south to the north of England in medieval times.
10351.statement: It took many weeks to travel from the south to the north of England in medieval times.
10351.correction: Harold and his housecarls were able to cover 185 miles in just four days in 1066: an amazing achievement.

9259.belief: The shield wall was not a very sophisticated or effective military tactic.
9259.statement: The shield wall was not a very sophisticated or effective military tactic.
9259.correction: In fact the shield wall proved effective in holding off the Norman attacks for many hours.

9187.belief: Sending the fyrd defences home in September is evidence of Harold's poor decision making.
9187.statement: Sending the fyrd defences home in September is evidence of Harold's poor decision making.
9187.correction: In fact, Anglo-Saxon leaders had always struggled with the 60-day limit for the fyrd. Harold had actually kept the fyrd out for twice as long as usual: evidence of his impressive influence as a leader.

4968.belief: The Norman conquest was fully achieved by the victory at the Battle of Hastings.
4968.statement: The Norman conquest was fully achieved by the victory at the Battle of Hastings.
4968.correction: In reality, there were many defiant Anglo-Saxons ready to carry on fighting and it took time for William to gain meaningful control over a hostile Anglo-Saxon population.

11007.belief: After William the Conqueror was crowned King of England, he and the Normans were immediately accepted as rightful rulers and peace reigned across the kingdom.
11007.statement: After William the Conqueror was crowned King of England, he and the Normans were immediately accepted as rightful rulers and peace reigned across the kingdom.
11007.correction: In fact, William faced a hostile Anglo-Saxon population and threats of invasion from Wales and Scotland, requiring him to take measures to establish further control.

1789.belief: A common misconception is that castles only had a military function.
1789.statement: A common misconception is that castles only had a military function.
1789.correction: Norman castles also acted as administrative centres. They had a psychological function in dominating the landscape and the people who lived there and some castles also helped trade develop.

8914.belief: Resistance to William’s rule of England came only from the English.
8914.statement: Resistance to William’s rule of England came only from the English.
8914.correction: In 1075, two Norman earls revolted against William, and English forces helped to stop the rebellion.

4538.belief: In the medieval period it was expected that rulers would be ruthless in killing anyone who opposed them.
