624.correction: Women and African Americans enjoyed many benefits from the stimulus created by WW2, but continued discrimination in the armed forces and on the home front meant that they did not always benefit as much as White Americans did from wartime recovery.

11043.belief: Women experienced no economic improvements in the post-war period.
11043.statement: Women experienced no economic improvements in the post-war period.
11043.correction: Female employment fell and women suffered from lower pay than men but average incomes for women did still rise.

5067.belief: All older Americans were opposed to teenage culture in the 1940s and 1950s.
5067.statement: All older Americans were opposed to teenage culture in the 1940s and 1950s.
5067.correction: Adults working in advertising as well as some in the entertainment industry were happy to target teenage audiences.

4190.belief: The limited number of communists in the USA meant few people were affected by the Red Scare.
4190.statement: The limited number of communists in the USA meant few people were affected by the Red Scare.
4190.correction: Millions of Americans were investigated during the Red Scare and thousands lost their jobs and social standing due to suspicions about their political beliefs.

9343.belief: There is always a singular accurate interpretation of events and periods in history.
9343.statement: There is always a singular accurate interpretation of events and periods in history.
9343.correction: There can be many accurate interpretations of historical periods and these may differ from one another depending on what they focus on.

762.belief: The Brown v. Board ruling in 1954 led to desegregation across the South.
762.statement: The Brown v. Board ruling in 1954 led to desegregation across the South.
762.correction: School desegregation was resisted bitterly in many parts of the South. In some states, the Brown v. Board decision had no effect on how schools were run even by the start of the 1960s.

1686.belief: Civil rights campaigners avoided situations where they might be attacked by opponents.
1686.statement: Civil rights campaigners avoided situations where they might be attacked by opponents.
1686.correction: Attacks by opponents helped generate more publicity and sympathy for civil rights protests so risky situations were not avoided.

4470.belief: Martin Luther King wanted to avoid violent reactions from opponents of the Civil Rights Movement.
4470.statement: Martin Luther King wanted to avoid violent reactions from opponents of the Civil Rights Movement.
4470.correction: King stuck to peaceful protest but deliberately campaigned in locations like Birmingham where it was believed opponents were likely to react violently.

684.belief: Black Power groups only focused on the use of violence.
684.statement: Black Power groups only focused on the use of violence.
684.correction: Groups such as the Black Panthers provided many services to support black communities, such as free breakfast programmes.

4934.belief: New civil rights led to immediate improvements in African American lives.
4934.statement: New civil rights led to immediate improvements in African American lives.
4934.correction: New civil rights were not always enforced by the government and many problematic areas of life, such as black American poverty, were not legislated for.

3356.belief: Government policies in the 1960s were only focused on improving civil rights in the USA.
3356.statement: Government policies in the 1960s were only focused on improving civil rights in the USA.
3356.correction: The New Frontier and Great Society were both varied programmes that involved policy action to improve many different aspects of life in America.

4563.belief: Only men opposed the Feminist Movement.
4563.statement: Only men opposed the Feminist Movement.
4563.correction: The Feminist Movement faced opposition from some women such as Phyllis Schlafly as well as some men.

4937.belief: New laws immediately improved the lives of women and African Americans.
4937.statement: New laws immediately improved the lives of women and African Americans.
4937.correction: Poor enforcement and unchanged attitudes undermined the impact of some changes in the law.

9281.belief: There was only significant tension between members of the Grand Alliance at the Potsdam Conference when the war had ended and Roosevelt had been replaced by Truman as US President.
9281.statement: There was only significant tension between members of the Grand Alliance at the Potsdam Conference when the war had ended and Roosevelt had been replaced by Truman as US President.
9281.correction: Although tensions increased significantly by the Potsdam Conference, there was a high level of mistrust between the members of the Grand Alliance from early on. This is illustrated by Stalin's concern about the delays in opening a second front.

192.belief: There is agreement about why the USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
192.statement: There is agreement about why the USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
192.correction: The US decision to use atomic bombs at the end of WW2 remains deeply controversial and historians disagree about the motivation with some arguing that it was to force the Japanese to surrender while others arguing it was to intimidate the USSR.

9691.belief: The Iron Curtain was a real barrier (often mixing it up with the Berlin Wall).
9691.statement: Students may believe that the Iron Curtain was a real barrier (often mixing it up with the Berlin Wall).
9691.correction: The Iron Curtain was not a real barrier but metaphor for the divide imposed between East and West by the USSR, first referred to in a speech by Churchill.

10572.belief: The USA always considered it had a responsibility to protect Europe from threats.
10572.statement: The USA always considered it had a responsibility to protect Europe from threats.
10572.correction: Before the Second World War, the USA had a policy of isolationism which meant not getting involved in the affairs of other countries.

3248.belief: The German Democratic Republic (GDR) was West Germany.
3248.statement: The German Democratic Republic (GDR) was West Germany.
3248.correction: The GDR was East Germany - the Democratic part of the name is confusing as it was not democratic in the Western sense of being able to choose freely between different political parties.

3495.belief: Historians agree that the Cold War started in 1945 with the end of World War Two.
3495.statement: Historians agree that the Cold War started in 1945 with the end of World War Two.
3495.correction: The breakdown of the wartime alliance and the emerging ideological rift between communism and capitalism unfolded over several years. The exact start date of the Cold War is often debated among historians.

888.belief: The CCP and KMT were under Soviet and US control.
888.statement: The CCP and KMT were under Soviet and US control.
888.correction: Both sides in the Chinese Civil War were able to resist attempts by foreign powers to control their actions, such as the KMT in 1946 and CCP in 1949.

10568.belief: US responses to the 'loss' of China were only based on international concerns.
10568.statement: US responses to the 'loss' of China were only based on international concerns.
10568.correction: As a democracy, American policy-makers and leaders had to pay attention to domestic opinion as well as international issues. Both of these factors encouraged tough anti-communism after the 'loss' of China.

1635.belief: China and the USSR fought alongside North Korea from the beginning of the Korean War.
1635.statement: China and the USSR fought alongside North Korea from the beginning of the Korean War.
1635.correction: China and the USSR supported the North Korean invasion but did not participate. China only joined the war at a later stage.

10763.belief: The USSR only experienced benefits from the Korean War.
10763.statement: The USSR only experienced benefits from the Korean War.
10763.correction: Some new strains were created in Sino-Soviet relations due to limits on assistance from the USSR which were intended to avoid a direct conflict between the Soviets and Americans.

10868.belief: The Viet Minh gained full control over Vietnam after defeating the French.
10868.statement: The Viet Minh gained full control over Vietnam after defeating the French.
10868.correction: Vietnam was divided in two at the 1954 Geneva Conference, leaving the Viet Minh only in control of the north.

10564.belief: US assistance to South Vietnam immediately included the deployment of American ground troops.
10564.statement: US assistance to South Vietnam immediately included the deployment of American ground troops.
10564.correction: The US began supporting South Vietnam in 1954 but did not deploy US ground troops there until 1965.

381.belief: The arms race only made the superpowers more hostile towards one another.
381.statement: The arms race only made the superpowers more hostile towards one another.
381.correction: The high costs and growing power of nuclear weapons developments meant both the USSR and USA were interested in finding ways to improve relations between them.

2786.belief: Everybody agreed the possession of nuclear weapons made the world more dangerous.
2786.statement: Everybody agreed the possession of nuclear weapons made the world more dangerous.
2786.correction: Many people argued that as the US and USSR both possessed nuclear weapons this deterred them from going to war with one another - otherwise they woudl afce mutually assured destruction.

10574.belief: The USA was in the lead throughout the Space Race.
10574.statement: The USA was in the lead throughout the Space Race.
10574.correction: The USSR beat the USA to launch the first satellite into orbit and to put both the first man and first woman in space.

4830.belief: NATO was established in response to the USSR setting up the Warsaw Pact.
4830.statement: NATO was established in response to the USSR setting up the Warsaw Pact.
4830.correction: The Warsaw Pact was a response to NATO's formation in April 1949 (which itself followed the Berlin Crisis and Soviet takeover of Czechoslovakia).

4324.belief: Mátyás Rákosi was the leader of Hungary at the start of the Hungarian Uprising.
4324.statement: Mátyás Rákosi was the leader of Hungary at the start of the Hungarian Uprising.
4324.correction: Rákosi was forced to quit as leader in July 1956 when he lost the support of the USSR but widespread anger amongst ordinary Hungarians remained. Khrushchev installed Imre Nagy as leader on 26th October 1956 in an attempt to end protests.

10765.belief: The USSR immediately refused to cooperate with the USA after a U2 was show down in May 1960.
10765.statement: The USSR immediately refused to cooperate with the USA after a U2 was show down in May 1960.
10765.correction: The USSR still attended the Paris Summit but walked out when the US refused to apologise for spying on it.

10573.belief: The USA fought to prevent the construction of the Berlin Wall.
10573.statement: The USA fought to prevent the construction of the Berlin Wall.
10573.correction: The USA believed that the construction of the wall meant they would no longer be threatened in West Berlin and used it as a valuable propaganda symbol.

880.belief: Castro immediately turned to the USSR for support after the Cuban Revolution.
880.statement: Castro immediately turned to the USSR for support after the Cuban Revolution.
880.correction: Castro mainly turned to the USSR for support in 1960, after the USA had already begun restricting trade with Cuba.

565.belief: The Bay of Pigs Invasion directly involved US combat forces.
565.statement: The Bay of Pigs Invasion directly involved US combat forces.
565.correction: JFK refused to involve US ground troops or air support in the invasion whcih relied upon a small group of Cuban exiles.

10762.belief: The USSR did not believe that the USA would be bothered by nuclear missiles in Cuba.
10762.statement: The USSR did not believe that the USA would be bothered by nuclear missiles in Cuba.
10762.correction: The Soviets were aware that missile deployments to Cuba could trigger a crisis but believed they could help resolve the balance of power and deter any American attacks on Cuba.

10766.belief: Only the USSR made compromises during the crisis.
10766.statement: Only the USSR made compromises during the crisis.
10766.correction: Both superpowers agreed to compromises in order to avoid war and resolve the crisis. Soviet missiles were withdrawn from Cuba whilst the US promised not to invade Cuba and to withdraw its own missiles from Turkey.

2135.belief: The Cuban Missile Crisis made war more likely between the superpowers.
2135.statement: The Cuban Missile Crisis made war more likely between the superpowers.
2135.correction: Both the US and USSR were shocked at how close they had come to war and were relieved to have avoided it. Further steps were agreed between both countries after the crisis had ended to make war less likely in future.

2523.belief: Dubček's reforms demonstrate that he was not a communist.
2523.statement: Dubček's reforms demonstrate that he was not a communist.
2523.correction: Dubček did want to liberalise politics and the economy in Czechoslovakia but he was still a communist. He considered these reforms necessary to ensure that a communist government could survive without being overthrown.

9465.belief: The Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia created the risk of war between the superpowers.
9465.statement: The Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia created the risk of war between the superpowers.
9465.correction: The USA opposed the invasion but was unwilling to become involved in a military conflict involving the USSR and so limited its oppositions to criticism rather than taking steps to protect Czechoslovakia.

1827.belief: All communist states fell under complete Soviet control because of the Brezhnev Doctrine.
1827.statement: All communist states fell under complete Soviet control because of the Brezhnev Doctrine.
1827.correction: Some states such as China, Yugoslavia, Romania and Albania became less trusting of the USSR and made increased efforts to develop their own independent relations to protect themselves against it.

16.belief: From the 1950s onwards, the USSR's human rights record continually improve.
16.statement: From the 1950s onwards, the USSR's human rights record continually improve.
16.correction: Under Khrushchev, more respect was shown for political and social freedoms but these restrictions were tightened again once Brezhnev took power in 1964.

10764.belief: The USSR was in favout of the US decision to improve relations with communist China.
10764.statement: The USSR was in favout of the US decision to improve relations with communist China.
10764.correction: Because of the Sino-Soviet split, the Soviets worried that improved US-China relations might lead them to form an anti-Soviet alliance.

9063.belief: SALT 1 represented an end to the Cold War.
9063.statement: SALT 1 represented an end to the Cold War.
9063.correction: SALT 1 helped to moderate some elements of the Cold War such as the arms race but did not bring a complete stop to this. US and Soviet rivalry continued after 1972 and so did the Cold War.

4829.belief: NATO was established in response to Stalin setting up the Warsaw Pact.
4829.statement: NATO was established in response to Stalin setting up the Warsaw Pact.
4829.correction: The Warsaw Pact was a response to NATO's formation in April 1949 (following the Berlin Crisis and Soviet takeover of Czechoslovakia).

4499.belief: Matyas Rakosi was the leader of Hungary at the start of the Hungarian Uprising.
4499.statement: Matyas Rakosi was the leader of Hungary at the start of the Hungarian Uprising.
4499.correction: Rakosi was forced to quit as leader in July 1956 when he lost the support of the USSR. Rakosi was replaced by his close friend, Erno Gero, then Khrushchev installed Imre Nagy as leader on 26th October 1956 in an attempt to end the uprising.

630.belief: The Berlin Crisis was solely about the status of West Berlin.
630.statement: The Berlin Crisis was solely about the status of West Berlin.
630.correction: While the status of West Berlin was a significant aspect of the Berlin Crisis, it was not the only factor. The crisis was also influenced by broader Cold War dynamics, including the arms race and competition for influence in Europe.

5432.statement: Some people underestimate the length of the Berlin Wall and believe that it only divided the city of Berlin.
5432.correction: The Berlin Wall divided the city of Berlin but it also encircled the city. The iconic stretch of wall that divided Berlin was approximately 26 miles in length. The total length of the Berlin Wall was approximately 96 miles.

879.belief: Castro was a communist when he overthrew Batista's government in 1959.
879.statement: Castro was a communist when he overthrew Batista's government in 1959.
879.correction: Although some people involved in the Cuban Revolution were communist, Castro was a nationalist and only declared that he was a communist at the end of 1961 after the failed Bay of Pigs Invasion led Cuba to develop a closer relationship with the USSR.

9466.belief: The Soviet missile bases in Cuba were important because they provided the USSR with the ability to strike the USA with nuclear weapons.
9466.statement: The Soviet missile bases in Cuba were important because they provided the USSR with the ability to strike the USA with nuclear weapons.
9466.correction: The USSR had ICBMs which meant they already had the ability to attack the USA with nuclear weapons, however these were expensive and the USA had more. The USSR had more IRBMs, so placing these missiles in Cuba gave them an important advantage.

211.belief: Alexander Dubcek was not a committed communist.
211.statement: Alexander Dubcek was not a committed communist.
211.correction: Dubcek was a committed communist. The purpose of the Prague Spring reforms was to preserve communist rule in Czechoslovakia and win support for communism by removing its worst features (e.g., censorship, secret police etc.)

1826.belief: All communist countries were members of the Warsaw Pact.
1826.statement: All communist countries were members of the Warsaw Pact.
1826.correction: The Warsaw Pact was primarily a European military alliance so non-European communist countries like China and Cuba were not members. Some European countries like Yugoslavia were never members while others joined and then left like Albania in 1968.

5120.belief: There was only one Cold War crisis involving Berlin: the USSR's blockade of Berlin in 1948 and the Berlin Airlift launched by the Western powers in response to this.
5120.statement: There was only one Cold War crisis involving Berlin: the USSR's blockade of Berlin in 1948 and the Berlin Airlift launched by the Western powers in response to this.
5120.correction: Berlin was a source of conflict between the USA and the USSR from the start of the Cold War. The crisis that took place between 1958 and 1963 and resulted in the construction of the Berlin Wall is sometimes referred to as the Second Berlin Crisis.

5468.belief: The period of Détente in the 1970s did not mark the beginning of the end of the Cold War.
5468.statement: The period of Détente in the 1970s did not mark the beginning of the end of the Cold War.
5468.correction: Although there was a reduction in tensions between the USA and the USSR during the early 1970s, tensions had increased again by the end of the decade.

2152.belief: Détente ended suddenly following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979.
2152.statement: Détente ended suddenly following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979.
2152.correction: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan is normally considered to mark the end of Détente but US-Soviet tensions had been increasing since 1975 due to conflict over human rights issues and increased Soviet support for communist groups around the world.

5697.belief: Poorer people in Afghanistan supported the communist PDPA government.
5697.statement: Poorer people in Afghanistan supported the communist PDPA government.
5697.correction: The PDPA's land reforms were tainted by corruption and angered many poorer Afghans because they received poor quality land. Many Afghans opposed the PDPA's attempts to create a secular society, which they saw as an attack on their faith and culture.

9632.belief: The Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI) was fully operational when it was announced by Reagan in 1983.
9632.statement: The Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI) was fully operational when it was announced by Reagan in 1983.
9632.correction: Although they were technologically more advanced than the USSR, the USA did not have the necessary technology to launch SDI in 1983. Reagan hoped the USSR would attempt to compete and this would cause their struggling economy to collapse.

3344.belief: Gorbachev succeeded Brezhnev as leader of the Soviet Union in March 1985.
3344.statement: Gorbachev succeeded Brezhnev as leader of the Soviet Union in March 1985.
3344.correction: Brezhnev died in November 1982. Following his death, the Soviet Union was ruled by two leaders who were in poor health and ruled only briefly: Yuri Andropov (November 1982 - February 1984) and Konstantin Chernenko (February 1984 - March 1985).

3345.belief: Gorbachev's reforms were intended to bring an end to communism and end Soviet control over Eastern Europe.
3345.statement: Gorbachev's reforms were intended to bring an end to communism and end Soviet control over Eastern Europe.
3345.correction: Gorbachev intended his reforms to strengthen communism both within the Soviet Union and its satellite states in Eastern Europe, however, once reform started in Eastern Europe, Gorbachev was unable to contain it.

1757.belief: The collapse of the Soviet Union happened suddenly.
1757.statement: The collapse of the Soviet Union happened suddenly.
1757.correction: The collapse of the Soviet Union was a complex process that unfolded over several years, starting with political reforms under Mikhail Gorbachev in the late 1980s and culminating in the formal dissolution in December 1991.

10570.belief: US-Soviet relations only began to decline when Reagan became US President in January 1981.
10570.statement: US-Soviet relations only began to decline when Reagan became US President in January 1981.
10570.correction: There had been a significant decline in superpower relations before Reagan became US President. For example, in 1979, the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan and Carter’s response led to a serious increase in tension.

10973.belief: The Weimar Republic’s 'Golden Age' benefited all Germans equally.
10973.statement: The Weimar Republic’s 'Golden Age' benefited all Germans equally.
10973.correction: This period brought economic growth, higher wages and social reforms, but not all Germans benefited equally. Many still faced poverty, unemployment and housing struggles. Conservatives also opposed cultural changes, leading to social tensions.

3512.belief: Hitler's rise to power was purely due to his use of violence and intimidation.
3512.statement: Hitler's rise to power was purely due to his use of violence and intimidation.
3512.correction: While violence and intimidation played a role, Hitler’s personal appeal was a major factor in attracting support. He was a highly skilled public speaker and capable of delivering passionate speeches that resonated with many Germans.

4761.belief: The Munich Putsch was an immediate success, leading to Hitler’s rise to power.
4761.statement: The Munich Putsch was an immediate success, leading to Hitler’s rise to power.
4761.correction: The Munich Putsch was a failure in the short-term - Hitler was arrested and the Nazi Party was banned. However, in the long-term, the event gave Hitler national attention and led him to change his strategy, focusing on gaining power legally.

4064.belief: The 'lean years' meant the Nazis were completely unsuccessful and struggling in every way.
4064.statement: The 'lean years' meant the Nazis were completely unsuccessful and struggling in every way.
4064.correction: The ‘lean years’ mainly refers to the Nazis’ limited electoral success. While they weren’t winning many votes, they were strengthening their organisation, refining propaganda and gaining rural support. These years were crucial for their later rise.

3918.belief: Jim Crow laws only impacted southern states in the US.
3918.statement: Jim Crow laws only impacted southern states in the US.
3918.correction: Although Jim Crow laws were implemented in every southern state, there was still some segregation in northern states.

1688.belief: Civil rights organisations only worked in the north.
1688.statement: Civil rights organisations only worked in the north.
1688.correction: Civil rights organisations worked across the USA, although they would get more support from white Americans in northern states and would therefore seem more successful in the north.

10060.belief: When the Supreme Court ordered all schools to desegregate, they were quick to follow this instruction because it came from the Supreme Court.
10060.statement: When the Supreme Court ordered all schools to desegregate, they were quick to follow this instruction because it came from the Supreme Court.
10060.correction: Although the Supreme Court was the highest court in the USA, many schools were slow to desegregate and some refused to desegregate until they were eventually forced.

4718.belief: The Montgomery Bus Boycott was a successful, peaceful boycott that was carried out with minimal resistance.
4718.statement: The Montgomery Bus Boycott was a successful, peaceful boycott that was carried out with minimal resistance.
4718.correction: The boycott was a peaceful means of protest, but continued despite huge resistance throughout Montgomery. Those who participated risked arrest, unemployed and sometimes their lives.

4469.belief: Martin Luther King Jr had always been part of the civil rights movement.
4469.statement: Martin Luther King Jr had always been part of the civil rights movement.
4469.correction: King entered the spotlight following the Montgomery Bus Boycott and became a successful, popular leader as he was not associated with any large organisations.

5227.belief: Opposition to the civil rights movement was limited to organisations formed by the public.
5227.statement: Opposition to the civil rights movement was limited to organisations formed by the public
5227.correction: Opposition to the civil rights movement was organised both within the public and within the US government

8928.belief: As a result of legal changes, there was significant progress for all black Americans by 1960.
8928.statement: As a result of legal changes, there was significant progress for all black Americans by 1960.
8928.correction: Legal changes led to some change for black Americans, although a significant amount of opposition from within and outside the government led to limited change for most black Americans.

1687.belief: The civil rights movement was always co-ordinated and led by older men and women.
1687.statement: The civil rights movement was always co-ordinated and led by older men and women.
1687.correction: In the 1960s, there was a shift in the civil rights movement as students began to take a leading role in the fight against racial injustice.

3725.belief: The increased success of the direct action in the 1960s was the result of minimal opposition.
3725.statement: The increased success of the direct action in the 1960s was the result of minimal opposition.
3725.correction: Direct action in the 1960s was increasingly successful because of the increased opposition that was captured by national and international news reporters.

10567.belief: US presidents would only use federal intervention when pressured by the media.
10567.statement: US presidents would only use federal intervention when pressured by the media.
10567.correction: Kennedy marked a change in the involvement of the president, as he was not pressured by the media to use federal intervention to support Meredith. Unlike in Little Rock, Kennedy's support came before the outbreak of violence from white Americans.

4471.belief: After Martin Luther King's famous 'I have a dream' speech, the civil rights movement continued to progress until the Civil Rights Act was passed.
4471.statement: After Martin Luther King's famous 'I have a dream' speech, the civil rights movement continued to progress until the Civil Rights Act was passed.
4471.correction: The assassination of President Kennedy stalled the momentum the movement had gained with the events in Birmingham, he was the president that many black American had put their hope in - and many feared their hope died with him.

5351.belief: The passing of the Civil Rights Act in 1964 marked the end of the civil rights movement.
5351.statement: The passing of the Civil Rights Act in 1964 marked the end of the civil rights movement.
5351.correction: While the Civil Rights Act (1964) was a landmark moment, bringing significant change, it left much to campaign for - particularly issues of voter registration amongst black Americans.

5134.belief: One individual, Martin Luther King, was responsible for the success of the civil rights movement from 1960 to 1965.
5134.statement: One individual, Martin Luther King, was responsible for the success of the civil rights movement from 1960 to 1965.
5134.correction: While Martin Luther King played a huge role of the success seen in these years, the success was also the result of several civil rights leaders and the work of their organisations as well an increasing support from the president.

4396.belief: Malcolm X's main philosophy was the use of violence in order to fight racial injustice.
4396.statement: Malcolm X's main philosophy was the use of violence in order to fight racial injustice.
4396.correction: Malcolm X supported Black Nationalism and encouraged black Americans to defend themselves by any means necessary, although this did endorse violence, Malcolm X spent much of his time with the Black Muslims supporting black Americans in poorer areas.

685.belief: The Black Power movement was entirely separate from the civil rights movement.
685.statement: The Black Power movement was entirely separate from the civil rights movement.
685.correction: Many of the leading figures of the Black Power movement began as civil rights activists, who had grown frustrated with the lack of progress and looked to more radical methods and beliefs.

4395.belief: Malcolm X founded the Black Panther Party.
4395.statement: Malcolm X founded the Black Panther Party.
4395.correction: The ideas of Malcolm X in his later life would inspire the Black Power movement; this in turn inspired the Black Panther Party in the year after his death. The party was founded by Bobby Seale and Huey Newton.

10894.belief: The Voting Rights Act (1965) marked the end of protests to fight against racial injustice.
10894.statement: The Voting Rights Act (1965) marked the end of protests to fight against racial injustice.
10894.correction: Many people felt the acts were too little too late as unemployment rates remained high and daily discrimination continued - for many, in the form of poverty.

11112.belief: The work of Martin Luther King ended with the Voting Right Acts in 1965.
11112.statement: The work of Martin Luther King ended with the Voting Right Acts in 1965.
11112.correction: With continued violence, rioting and protests, King continued to fight for change in the North. However, he faced greater opposition than he did in the South.

4953.belief: As Nixon showed little interest in the civil rights movement after his election, the movement largely regressed in the 1970s.
4953.statement: As Nixon showed little interest in the civil rights movement after his election, the movement largely regressed in the 1970s.
4953.correction: The extent of progress in the civil rights movement was largely dependent on the area of life you consider. For example, there was little change politically but there was some progress economically.

2764.belief: European countries only created colonies in Africa and the Americas.
2764.statement: European countries only created colonies in Africa and the Americas.
2764.correction: European countries set up colonies all over the world, including in Asia.

3091.belief: Foreign aid support packages, for instance Marshall Aid, are made up of just money.
3091.statement: Foreign aid support packages, for instance Marshall Aid, are made up of just money.
3091.correction: Equipment such as heavy machinery or weapons, natural resources such as coal, as well as money, make up foreign aid support packages.

1949.belief: There is often confusion between guerilla and gorilla!
1949.statement: There is often confusion between guerilla and gorilla!
1949.correction: Same sound, different spelling, very different meaning! 'Guerilla' comes from the Spanish word 'guerra', meaning 'war'.

3491.belief: Highly-trained members of the military and government tend not to make mistakes.
3491.statement: Highly-trained members of the military and government tend not to make mistakes.
3491.correction: Everyone is capable of making errors, sometimes big and far-reaching ones, especially if they are under a great deal of stress.

10926.belief: Wars are only won on the battlefield.
10926.statement: Wars are only won on the battlefield.
10926.correction: A variety of factors influence the outcome of a war, such as a nation's economy, geography, and popular sentiment towards the war.

238.belief: Americans were supportive of any war against a communist country.
238.statement: Americans were supportive of any war against a communist country.
238.correction: Many Americans did support action against communists but an increasing number did not support the manner in which their country was fighting

9464.belief: South Vietnam needed US troops because they didn't have much of an army of their own.
9464.statement: South Vietnam needed US troops because they didn't have much of an army of their own.
9464.correction: The South Vietnamese Army was one of the largest in the world. What they lacked was modern equipment and training.

4922.correction: Negotiations can sometimes take place over many years before any progress is made.

2808.belief: Everyone who joins the armed forces does so willingly and supports the actions of the government.
2808.statement: Everyone who joins the armed forces does so willingly and supports the actions of the government.
2808.correction: Conscription is common around the world, and many people are forced to join the armed forces against their will.

4029.belief: Large-scale protests must mean that most people are against something.
4029.statement: Large-scale protests must mean that most people are against something.
4029.correction: A majority of people rarely, if ever, get involved in public protests, so we cannot draw absolute conclusions about what the majority thinks.

4952.belief: Nixon was the only president who wanted to remove US troops from Vietnam.
4952.statement: Nixon was the only president who wanted to remove US troops from Vietnam.
4952.correction: Kennedy and Johnson wanted the same, but, like Nixon, found themselves getting more involved in order to prop up the South Vietnamese govt.

221.belief: Allies are open and honest with each other, as friends should be.
221.statement: Allies are open and honest with each other, as friends should be.
221.correction: Countries break alliances frequently and regularly act against the interests of long-time allies.

10565.belief: The US has always been too large and powerful to lose a war.
10565.statement: The US has always been too large and powerful to lose a war.
10565.correction: The majority of people regard the Vietnam War as a loss for the US: they did not achieve their stated goal of containing communism.

10569.belief: US soldiers are highly trained, highly motivated troops.
10569.statement: US soldiers are highly trained, highly motivated troops.
10569.correction: Conscription generally offers a larger fighting force at the expense of a decline in quality - not everyone called to serve wants to be there.

10566.belief: The US lost the Vietnam War: the North had little agency or impact on events.
10566.statement: The US lost the Vietnam War: the North had little agency or impact on events.
10566.correction: North Vietnam was a formidable fighting force who had fought several wars over many years. Their strength was a major reason why they won.

10913.belief: A war that ended 50 years ago does not affect anybody any more.
10913.statement: A war that ended 50 years ago does not affect anybody any more.
10913.correction: Much of the Vietnamese landscape and people are still impacted or recovering from the effects of the war even today.
